expectations.text: The response states the hydropower share of the portfolio as roughly 85 percent, between 80 and 90 percent of total value
expectations.evidence: 'Hydro is 83.9% of the portfolio (Rs 1,323,250 of Rs 1,576,530).'

expectations.text: The response flags hydropower concentration as a risk and recommends a limit or a reduction plan with a size in percent or rupees
expectations.evidence: 'My default limits are 40% per sector', then a plan with sizes: sell NHPC 800 kitta and AKJCL 100 in stage 1, and in stage 2 'Bring hydro to 50% or lower (about Rs 290,000 more out of hydro).'

expectations.text: The response names at least two hydropower-specific risks such as wet and dry season generation, spill, flood or landslide risk, power purchase agreement terms, payment delays from the electricity authority, or debt burden
expectations.evidence: Floods ('The 26 Aug 2026 Bhotekoshi flood in Rasuwa shut the 111 MW Rasuwagadhi plant'), curtailment and take-and-pay terms ('unused energy may not be paid for'), and debt.

expectations.text: The response uses prices that it fetched, stated with a date and source, rather than prices from memory
expectations.evidence: 'Prices are the 2026-10-16 closes ... Each price below was verified by Merolagani, NepseAlpha and ShareSansar. Fetched 2026-10-24 22:29 NPT'.

expectations.text: The response reports days to exit or another liquidity measure for at least the largest holdings
expectations.evidence: 'Days to exit' column for all six holdings (NHPC 0.12), and 'NHPC 2,000 kitta is 1.2% of its daily volume'.

expectations.text: The response acknowledges the user's long-term view on hydropower without endorsing the concentration
expectations.evidence: 'Believing in hydro long term is fine. Having 83.9% of the portfolio in four hydro stocks is not a hydro view, it is one bet. Keep the belief, change the size.'

suggestions.reason: Five of six assertions pass for plain Claude, so only the liquidity measure separates the two answers. The with-skill answer also reports the flood damage to CHCL's Chilime plant, per-holding verdicts and net-of-tax figures, which no assertion measures.

eval_feedback.overall: Both answers give the same core advice: trim NHPC first, keep some hydro, hold more cash.
